x: Even in the Men's Cross Country we have a new star in Kaesse Tadesse who warmed the hearts of many on a freezing day at Parliament Hill with his second place in the Junior race.
Halfway. Tim Dickinson (Blackheath) and Kaessa Tadesse run shoulder to shoulder with Spencer Barden (GEC Avionics) and Stefan White (Coventry Godiva) right on their tails.
Front page: Kasse Tadesse leads the field into the back stretch mid-way through the 10,000 metres in the European Clubs Championship at the U.T.E stadium, Budapest.

Kasse Tadesse gave us a silver medal in the National Junior CC Champs. but we were relegated to the second division in our league. Our ladies, however, took great delight in fighting their way up their league and already this winter they have shaken the opposition in Surrey Division One.
With a 2:19 marathon in his legs Kasse Tadesse appeared to be taking the 5 mile Junior race very comfortably, loping along behind Mole Valley's Bruno Witchells.
Chandler's Ford, 2 May. 10k: 13, M.Webb 33:00. Dublin, 2 May. 5m: Kasse Tadesse placed 5th in 23:33 behind a quartet of talented Kenyans who were spearheaded by Ishmael Kirui, 22:08.

The Kenyan pair of Masya and Miano sped through the opening mile in 4:18 with Kasse Tadesse heading the rest, Two miles came up in 8:40 and then Gary was sharing the lead with Miano and Ireland's John Treacy at '3' in 13:12.

From left to right, standing: Leo Coy, John Wilson, Kasse Tadesse, Toby Earle, Marcello Bizio, Rob Milner, Stuart Booth, Roger Alsop, John Booth, Cross Country Captain Graham Adams, ?, Charlie Dickinson, Colin Pearson, Steve Willimont, Trevor Williams, Mike Webb, Larry McLean, ?, Marlon Anderson, Ma…
But what about Kasse Tadesse? As a 10 and 5k man he is only ever likely to compete in just one event at these meetings - and yet he got up to no. 3.

Kasse Tadesse won his first marathon in Livorno, Italy, on November 14th in 2 hours 19 minutes 14 seconds. Still only nineteen years of age, this man is going to be one of the all-time greats if he continues in this vein.

Kasse Tadesse had great difficulty in restraining himself, throwing in fast and slow laps with a complete disregard for the opposition. Even Boutayeb must have been wondering who this young man was when a circuit in the low 60s was injected around the 5k point.
Kasse Tadesse has supported the Club well during his first season and indeed ran his first ever 5000m and 10000m on the track in Belgrave colours.

Kasse Tadesse made a winning début in the 5000m, running from the front in windy conditions. But pride of place must go to 16 year-old Gavin Mason who was drafted into the 'B' 800 as a last minute replacement.
Kasse Tadesse, Paul Edwards and Leith Marar repeated their first match wins with Paul again covering gaps, this time the 'B' javelin. Ian Tullett won the pole vault as Mike Edwards no-heighted.

In the middle distance events Kasse Tadesse returned to winning ways with a pb in the 5000m but despite all our efforts it was 3rd spot on the day but with the satisfaction that we were a clear second in the league some four league points clear of Birchfield.
